sentences.text: Yacarerani is an extinct genus of notosuchian crocodylomorph, a group of crocodile-like reptiles, from the Late Cretaceous.
This small crocodylomorph measured approximately 80 cm in length.

It possessed heterodont dentition, featuring different tooth shapes in different parts of the jaws, including two teeth in the lower jaw that projected forward from the tip, resembling rabbit incisors.
Two teeth in the lower jaw projected forward from the tip, resembling rabbit incisors.
Fossil material representing two individuals was found in association with eggs believed to be part of a nest.
Fossils of Yacarerani were found in 2002 in the Cajones Formation of Amboró National Park in central Bolivia and date to the Turonian-Santonian stages.
The genus Yacarerani was formally described in 2009 in the Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology.
Researchers suggest Yacarerani may have lived in small groups and created burrows to lay eggs.
A 2026 study by Navarro et al. interprets the bone histology of Yacarerani boliviensis as consistent with fast growth dynamics interrupted by periods of decline.
The time range for Yacarerani is recorded as Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago).
